args.notes: Answer: ilovedavidverve — the -p argument of the root-executed useradd that created user tomcat7 on hoth. Chain: hoth is the only non-EC2 Linux host with shell history and osquery telemetry (bash_history host breakdown: hoth=/home/klagerfield/.bash_history; gacrux/mars EC2 hosts=ec2-user histories). On hoth, osquery pack_process-monitoring_proc_events recorded two useradd executions for user tomcat7: 19:08:05 by tomcat8 (uid=111, euid=111 — non-root, would fail) with -p davidverve.com, and 19:24:54 by root (uid=0, euid=0, gid=0, egid=0) with -p ilovedavidverve, options -ou tomcat7 0 -g 0 -M -N -r -s /bin/bash (UID 0 backdoor account with bash shell). The root-run one is the successful creation the question names; its password argument is the answer. Residual gap (why confidence is 85, not higher): I found no independent post-creation artifact naming tomcat7 on hoth — Unix:UserAccounts covers only gacrux EC2 hosts (0 events for hoth), and tomcat7 does not appear in hoth's osquery last/logged_in_users/shell_history packs. The success of the root-run useradd rests on it executing as uid=0, which is the act itself, not on a separate confirmation record. The 4 shell_history keyword matches from round 2 turned out to be auditctl/ausearch commands watching /etc/passwd, not password-setting. Note useradd -p normally expects an encrypted hash; the attacker passed the plaintext string, which is what the question asks to return 'exactly as recorded'.
